repairs: Explicit-range sequential continuation and same-read source identity.
Underscore component matching prevents discovery/selection mismatch.
Standalone literal symbol queries suppress partial namesakes.
Sparse locator catalogs avoid advice naming unavailable tools.
Precise follow-ups, now exposed by read_code, preserve explicit scopes, sequential continuation and same-read fingerprints; invalid scopes fail rather than widening.
Literal named definitions survive candidate cutoff; complete definitions use exact rendered eligibility and compatible overlaps preserve both sides.
Query-only search_code accounts for JSON escaping under the unchanged context cap; read_code retains explicit-follow-up pricing.
Discovery and known-path reading have separate opt-in contracts; scope errors suggest discovery without automatic fallback or scope widening.
Explicitly qualified definition sources outrank mention-only matches without changing schemas, selectors or context budgets.
The opt-in split rejects unknown arguments in schemas and execution, so removed search_code scopes cannot be silently ignored.

limitations: One answering model and Python repositories.
Repeatedly reused ten-question development set; not evidence of general superiority.
Fourth-study reserved questions were historically reused; its validation failed.
New question dataset reuses repositories and is not a claim of unseen model training data.
Lower source-body tokens or fewer tool calls do not establish lower cumulative provider tokens.
